title: The First Picture of a Black Hole

anim.title: A puzzle
items: A black hole lets no light out
So how do you photograph one?

segments.say: A black hole lets no light escape. So how do you take its photograph?
Like this. In April twenty nineteen, scientists showed the world the first picture of a black hole: a dark shadow inside a ring of glowing gas.

anim.title: What you're seeing
items: Hot gas swirling around it glows
The black hole's shadow sits in the middle
The ring is light bent by gravity

segments.say: The ring is hot gas swirling around the black hole, its light bent by gravity. The dark centre is the black hole's shadow.
This one sits in the galaxy Messier eighty-seven, fifty-five million light-years away, and weighs six and a half billion Suns.
No single telescope is big enough. So radio dishes across the world watched together, timed by atomic clocks, acting like one telescope the size of the Earth.

items.text: Sagittarius A*, our own galaxy's black hole

segments.say: In twenty twenty-two, the same team showed the black hole at the centre of our own galaxy, Sagittarius A star.
For Prelims: Event Horizon Telescope, radio dishes linked across the Earth. M87 star in twenty nineteen, Sagittarius A star in twenty twenty-two.

sources: Event Horizon Telescope press release, 10 April 2019: first image of the black hole in M87, 55 million light-years away, 6.5 billion solar masses; array of radio telescopes linked by very-long-baseline interferometry with atomic clocks
EHT / ESO press release eso2208-eht-mw, 12 May 2022: first image of Sagittarius A*, the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way
Picture: 'Black hole - Messier 87' from the EHT Collaboration, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

quiz.q: Which black hole was the first ever photographed?
How did the EHT get Earth-sized sharpness?
options: Very long exposures from one site
quiz.why: Linked dishes act like one Earth-sized telescope.

quiz.q: What does the bright ring show?
options: Glowing gas, its light bent by gravity
quiz.why: The shadow sits inside a ring of hot gas.

reviewNote: Facts were read against the EHT press releases of April 2019 and May 2022. Picture is the EHT image under CC BY 4.0. Moving facts: none.
